title: Unexplained Delay or Workaround Hacks
pattern: Adding a workaround or hack comment (e.g., hardcoded sleeps, retries) without explaining the technical rationale or timing issue being addressed.
why_bad: Fosters 'voodoo programming.' Future developers are forced to leave fragile hacks untouched because they cannot verify what boundary condition or race the delay is shielding.
detection: Comments describing an operational workaround (such as a hardcoded `sleep` or retry loop) without specifying the upstream bug, race condition, or hardware register manual references.
counterexample: A sleep documented with the precise constraint: 'controller chip reset self-test takes 40ms per hardware manual section 4.2.'
fix: Document the precise hardware register reference, upstream issue ID, or timing constraint justifying the workaround.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Differentiate between major and minor comments"); Dustin Boswell & Trevor Foucher, *The Art of Readable Code* (2012), Chapter 5 ("Include \"Director Commentary\"").
